case_study_packaging.headline: Christianbook trims $1.24 million in annual indirect spend and nets a 3.3× ROI through Treya’s strategic sourcing program
case_study_packaging.client_problem_statement: Christianbook, a multichannel retailer of Christian books and gifts, relied on long-standing supplier relationships and a largely decentralized purchasing model. With private-equity ownership seeking to boost enterprise value, leadership needed a rapid, data-driven way to uncover and capture savings across freight, payments, packaging, and other indirect categories. Limited internal bandwidth, incomplete vendor data, and the risk of disrupting customer fulfillment made outside expertise essential.
case_study_packaging.client_problem_anonymized: A multichannel faith-based retailer relied on long-standing supplier relationships and a largely decentralized purchasing model. With the private equity ownership group focused on operational efficiency and margin improvement, leadership needed a rapid, data-driven way to uncover and capture savings across freight, payments, packaging, and other indirect categories. Limited internal bandwidth, incomplete vendor data, and the risk of disrupting customer fulfillment made outside expertise essential.
approach_summary: Performed a forensic 12-month AP spend analysis covering eight indirect categories totaling $18 M, prioritizing $9.2 M for immediate action.
Launched competitive RFPs underpinned by Treya market benchmarks for merchant processing, LTL/FTL freight, corrugated cartons, and shipping supplies.
Transitioned card processing to Calibr and freight to Echo Logistics, orchestrating zero-downtime cutovers while negotiating best-in-class rates.
Re-negotiated with incumbent packaging suppliers and added a third partner to unlock volume-based price breaks without changing product specifications.
Implemented spend dashboards, supplier scorecards, and communication protocols to institutionalize strategic sourcing discipline for future waves.
case_study_packaging.value_delivered_blurb: Treya delivered $1,237,359 in fully-finalized annual savings—an average 13.4 % reduction that slightly exceeded the high end of the original estimate. The engagement generated a 3.3× return on Treya’s fixed $375K fee while enhancing cost transparency, supplier performance management, and procurement governance that will fuel additional future savings.
where_we_were_unique: Exceeded the client’s own high-end savings projection by leveraging real-time market benchmarks.
Drove a 31 % LTL freight reduction without service disruption by executing a well-planned carrier switch during peak season.
Balanced savings with relationship continuity—retaining preferred suppliers in key categories while still securing double-digit price cuts.
Realized first contract signatures and savings within roughly six months, accelerating EBITDA impact ahead of the next budgeting cycle.
